This unevenness in the location of the poor partly reflects the size of populations across economies. A dissimilarity index has been developed to measure the extent to which the concentration of poverty exceeds estimates based on population size alone if poverty rates were evenly distributed across economies by population size (refer to annex 1D). If an economy has a share of the global poor that is equal to its share of the global population, the index is 0. The closer the index is to 1, the more skewed poverty is relative to an economy’s population size.
